Extract RAP vegetation cover for polygons

Source: R/extract_rap.R
extract_rap.Rd

Returns the mean percent cover of each Rangeland Analysis Platform (RAP) vegetation cover v3 band inside every feature of geometry.

Usage

extract_rap(
  year,
  geometry,
  cover = names(RAP_BANDS),
  units = c("ha", "km2", "m2", "acres", "mi2"),
  id = NULL,
  wide = FALSE,
  cache_dir = NULL,
  chunk_size = 500L,
  workers = 4L,
  cores = 1L,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

year

Integer, 1986 to 2025.

geometry

An sf/sfc object, a terra::SpatVector, or a path to any vector file sf::st_read() can open. Polygons only. Must fall within CONUS.

cover

Cover types to return, as RAP band codes: any of "AFG" (annual forb and grass), "BGR" (bare ground), "LTR" (litter), "PFG" (perennial forb and grass), "SHR" (shrub), "TRE" (tree). Case insensitive. Defaults to all 6.

units

Area units: one of "ha", "km2", "m2", "acres", "mi2".

id

Optional column name in geometry to use as the feature id. Defaults to row number.

wide

If TRUE, return one row per feature with pct_<band> and area_<band> columns. Default FALSE returns long (tidy) format.

cache_dir

Directory for cached tiles. Defaults to a persistent user cache (tools::R_user_dir("fastrap", "cache")).

chunk_size

Features per chunk. Lower it if memory is tight.

workers

Parallel download workers. Raise it on a fast connection.

cores

Worker processes for extraction (forked; Unix/macOS only, ignored on Windows).

quiet

Suppress progress messages.

Value

A data.frame. Long format columns: id, year, band (RAP band code: AFG, BGR, LTR, PFG, SHR, TRE), cover_type, pct (area-weighted mean percent cover over the feature's cells with data), and area (pct / 100 times the feature's area, in units). Bands do not sum to 100: RAP predicts each cover type separately.

Details

Speed comes from four things:

  • Only the 2048 x 2048 pixel windows of the national cloud-optimized GeoTIFF that touch your features are read, using HTTP range requests. Nothing national is downloaded.

  • Windows are fetched by parallel workers (works on Windows too) and cached on disk, so repeat calls over the same area skip the network.

  • Windows snap to the RAP grid, so no resampling happens.

  • Extraction uses exact, cell-area-weighted coverage fractions (exactextractr, C++).

Memory stays flat for large layers: features are sorted spatially and run in chunks of chunk_size, and each chunk reads only its own tiles through a lazy VRT.

RAP was built for rangelands. Its authors note cover estimates may not suit forests or agricultural land.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
nc <- sf::st_read(system.file("shape/nc.shp", package = "sf"))
extract_rap(year = 2024, geometry = nc[1:5, ], units = "km2", id = "NAME")
extract_rap(2024, nc[1:5, ], cover = c("TRE", "SHR"), id = "NAME")
} # }
